messages.subject: Conditional markup blocks?
messages.body_snippet:
Hello,

Does anyone know if it is possible to conditionally knit blocks of markdown, etc.?

For example, it would be nice to be able to do something like:

```{r start}
if (x == TRUE) {
```
some text

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Conditional markup blocks?
messages.body_plain:
You can make use of child documents.

```{r main}
x = TRUE # or FALSE
```

Then

```{r test, child = if (x == TRUE) 'child-a.Rmd' else 'child-b.Rmd'}
```

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: RStudio/knitr/pandoc HTML slides with traditional graphics?
messages.subject_clean: RStudio/knitr/pandoc HTML slides with traditional graphics?
messages.body_plain:
Greetings.  I noticed that by using RStudio/knitr/pandoc one can create HTML
slides from R Markdown files.  This seems very convenient, but I've had
problems with my first attempt at it.

I don't seem to be able to use traditional graphics to make slides.  I've
tried a number of variations on this, but I think the following sums it up.

I took Yihui's example file, 009-slides.Rmd, and modified it to contain a
short section with a traditional plot command:

$ diff 009-slides.Rmd knitr-examples/009-slides.Rmd
32,38d31
< # What about traditional graphics?
< ```{r tradGraph, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
<
< plot(rnorm(100))
<
< ```
<

I converted the modified file using pandoc:

$ pandoc -s -S -i -t dzslides --mathjax 009-slides.md -o \
    009-slides-converted.html

When I view 009-slides-converted.html, I see everything, including the figure
produced by "qplot" in the "Graphics too" section, EXCEPT that all I see on my
"What about traditional graphics?" slide is the R command:

    plot(rnorm(100))

on an otherwise completely black background.  Can somebody tell me what I'm
doing wrong?

Note that I've tried many variations of this with different figure sizes, etc.
Everything always displays fine in the HTML preview, for instance.  Nothing
makes the final, converted-to-slides version any better.

All of the relevant software is pretty current.  Please see the appended for
some details.

Thanks.

-- Mike

Try changing your plotting colors, or specify a non-transparent background for the plot (possibly using par(bg='white') or you may need to set an option to the graphics device). To get rCharts to work with knit2html, you will need to use the print method with the argument include_assets = TRUE. This is because knitr will not add the js and css assets required by an rCharts plot automatically. Here is a minimal working example.

## MorrisJS with Knit2HTML

```{r results = 'asis', comment = NA}
require(rCharts)
data(economics, package = 'ggplot2')

m1 <- mPlot(x = 'date', y = c('psavert', 'uempmed'), type = 'Line',
  data = econ)
m1$set(pointSize = 0, lineWidth = 1)
m1$print('chart2', include_assets = TRUE)
```

Note that you need to use m1$print('chart2', include_assets = TRUE, cdn = TRUE) if you intend to publish your chart on RPubs, for otherwise the JS and CSS assets will be served from your local library.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] multiple tables in knitr
messages.body_plain:
The key to tables with knitr is the chunk option results='asis', and
you are right that tables are not as well supported as graphics. You
will have to go with a few more keystrokes if you want to put more
than one table in one table environment. Just remember if you use
packages like xtable to create tables, be sure not to generate the
code for the table environment (i.e. print(xtable, floating = FALSE)).
I do not recognize a "canonical" way for this.

If you use the latest development version of knitr
(https://github.com/yihui/knitr#readme), I have an experimental
function kable() that generates "barebone" tables, e.g.

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

\begin{table}
\caption{A tale of two tables.}
<<test, results='asis'>>=
library(knitr)
kable(head(iris))
kable(head(mtcars[, 1:5]))
@
\end{table}

\end{document}

Tables are not fun to work with, and that is probably the reason why
they have low priority in knitr :)

Regards,
Yihui
